findings.location: §5.C closing paragraph ('Summed: no AmbientCapabilities, no sudo, no root anywhere in the fleet. The complete privilege surface is system-bus socket access, optionally the session bus via the Environment block, and the existing polkit rule pattern...') and §6 'Mesh/exit-node health' paragraph
findings.finding: The draft claims a COMPLETE zero-root privilege surface but never addresses the tailscaled leg that backend-headscale requires. backend-headscale shells to `tailscale status --json` (per the interim report; the draft itself scopes it to europa's server role in §1 and Phase 3's 'version-tolerant headscale parsing'), and the corpus holds the sanctioned unprivileged mechanism the summed surface omits: `tailscale set --operator=<user>` designates a non-root user allowed to operate tailscaled, plus the `--socket=<path>` global flag for NixOS hosts where the socket path is customised. Without the operator designation the headscale backend breaks the 'no root anywhere' claim as written. The corpus also holds the rest of the operational surface the mesh paragraph ignores while every sibling feature gap (SMART, ZFS, backlight) gets its mechanism named: `tailscale wait` / tailscale-online.target as the official readiness gate for services binding to the tailnet (the precise ordering unit where mesh reachability, not network-online.target, gates the agent), `BackendState` from `status --json` as the reliable running-indicator with a fail-fast exit-code pattern, `netcheck --format=json` as a machine-readable network-quality sensor, `version --json/--daemon/--upstream` for three-way client-drift detection, and the upstream recognition that bare `--json` output is version-frozen-by-policy (the draft's 'unstable-by-policy' phrasing) with a proposed versioned contract an agent-side schema check can rely on.
findings.suggested_fix: Two surgical inserts. (1) In §5.C, after the 'Summed:' sentence, add the missing leg: 'One leg the sum must name: backend-headscale shells to `tailscale status --json`, and unprivileged operation of tailscaled is a designation, not a default — `tailscale set --operator=io` is the sanctioned grant, with `--socket=<path>` covering NixOS's customised socket location [[tailscale-cli-tailscale-docs]].' (2) In §6's mesh paragraph, after 'the parser is version-tolerant', add one sentence matching the depth of the SMART/ZFS paragraphs: 'The operational surface around the schema: `tailscale wait` / tailscale-online.target is the official readiness gate where mesh reachability orders the agent; `BackendState` (checked fail-fast, distinct exit codes) is the reliable running-indicator; and upstream's frozen-version-1 `--json` contract means the version-tolerance is a schema check, not a re-parse.'

findings.location: §6 JupiterOS-Specific Feature Gaps (absent — no power/UPS item among the enumerated gaps: systemd, SMART, ZFS, mesh, generation, reboot, notifications, boost, desktop)
findings.finding: The corpus holds a seven-claim NUT cluster that the draft uses zero times, and the pipeline itself flagged it: comparisons.md lists [[network-ups-tools-nut-home-assistant]] as 'the HA-side shape a fleet UPS sensor set should mirror', and loci.json carries it in the privilege-ladder locus's corpus_evidence. The claims define both the architecture (the HA NUT integration cannot talk to a UPS directly — a NUT server is required, NUT protocol on port 3493, 60-second default polling) and the ceilings a fleet design must know: it can retrieve but not set NUT variables and does not support parameterised commands; device actions (instcmds like beeper.disable, test.battery.start.quick, power-cycle outlet) require credentialled upsd.users grants; it cannot auto-detect a server IP change (DNS-name resolution, never baked IPs); most diagnostic sensors are disabled by default as a deliberate recorder-cost trim; and the raw surface an agent should consume is enumerable via `upsc`/`upscmd`. The draft's §6 preamble claims 'each item maps to a host class in the fleet's configurations' — power monitoring maps to the server role (europa, the HPE MicroServer NAS) and is simply missing, with no audited-absence statement either (the deep-inference standard requires naming what was searched: whether any jupiterOS host declares a UPS).
findings.suggested_fix: Either add one §6 paragraph in server-class voice using the corpus claims — 'Power/UPS (europa; conditional): the HA-native shape is NUT — server-required, port 3493, 60-second polling, instcmds gated on credentialled upsd.users, no set-variable support — so an agent-side consumer enumerates `upsc`/`upscmd` directly, resolves the server by DNS name (the integration cannot survive an IP change), and trims its entity surface as deliberately as NUT trims its diagnostics' — or, if no fleet host declares a UPS, add the audited-absence sentence to §6's preamble: 'Power/UPS is absent from every jupiterOS host configuration (searched: hosts/, modules/ for ups/nut/apc declarations) — NUT remains the shape the day one is attached.' Do not leave the cluster unused either way; comparisons.md already committed it to the draft.

findings.location: §3 'The identity and notification bars' ('giving an MQTT-only agent a first-class `notify.<device>` service, strictly better than the current payload-hack button, implementable today') and §6 'Notifications, end to end'
findings.finding: The notify.mqtt confirmation chain (PR #115653 + test payload + const.py) is used, but two corpus notes completing that chain are dropped, and one carries a ceiling the advocate register should name: the 2024.5 notify model is an ENTITY platform, and entity-platform notifiers are not visible to legacy notify-SERVICE consumers — the HA community thread documents notify entities (mqtt notify among them) being unusable as the legacy alert integration's notifier, forcing notify.send_message with entity_id targeting. The draft's 'first-class notify.<device> service' phrasing reads as the legacy service shape the corpus contradicts. The second unused note is the notify.py source itself (async_setup_entity_entry_helper + MqttEntity wiring, command_topic required), which is the fourth leg of the confirmation chain (the draft cites PR, test, and const.py) and the primary-source proof that discovery-registered notify entities are first-class MQTT entities — evidence that strengthens the very claim it qualifies.
findings.suggested_fix: In §3, after 'implementable today', insert the qualifier with both citations: '— with one named ceiling: notify.mqtt lands as a notify ENTITY (targeted via notify.send_message with entity_id), and legacy notify-service consumers such as the alert integration cannot target entity notifiers directly, so alert-style consumers take the automation route [[notification-entities-and-alert-integration-configuration-home-assistant-communi]]; the notify.py source (MqttEntity via async_setup_entity_entry_helper) is the primary-source leg of the confirmation chain [[corehomeassistantcomponentsmqttnotifypy-at-dev-home-assistantcore-github]].' Optionally adjust 'first-class notify.<device> service' to 'first-class notify entity' for accuracy.

findings.location: §6 'The future desktop host class' ('its boundary is solved from source: the compositor's IPC socket is created as niri.{wayland_socket_name}.{pid}.sock ... so a same-UID User=io system service reaches it by globbing, no session unit required')
findings.finding: The draft cites two of the three niri source notes (the socket formula and the event-stream contract) but drops the third: the security model. niri's own documentation warns 'Anything with access to niri's IPC socket can, among other things: Spawn a Wayland client — which in turn can record the screen, emulate input, read the clipboard, spoof password dialogs via layer-shell'. The paragraph presents same-UID socket reach as purely a convenience ('no session unit required') while claiming the boundary is 'solved from source' — but the security model IS part of the boundary, and for a control-plane daemon it is the threat-surface statement: a compromised agent running as io gains kiosk screen capture and input emulation through the very socket the design celebrates. The corpus also holds the cleaner reach mechanism the draft's 'globbing' glosses over: the niri-ipc client library resolves the socket via NIRI_SOCKET and accepts an explicit path via connect_to(). In a report whose §5.C thesis is 'the privilege design and the feature design are the same document', omitting the one interface with a documented security cost is a one-sided treatment.
findings.suggested_fix: In §6's desktop paragraph, after 'no session unit required', insert: '— with the security cost named alongside the convenience: niri's own model warns that IPC-socket access means spawning a Wayland client that can record the screen, emulate input, and read the clipboard, so the agent's socket reach is a privileged capability in practice and belongs in the same threat model as the polkit grants [[security-model-niri-wmniri-wiki-github]]; the explicit-path connect_to() (or NIRI_SOCKET) is the cleaner reach than globbing [[niriniri-ipcsrcsocketrs-at-main-niri-wmniri-github]].'

findings.location: §5.C SMART bullet and §6 'SMART/NVMe (europa; opt-in elsewhere)' paragraph
findings.finding: The SMART treatment (smartd hook + capability ceilings) is present but the corpus holds four load-bearing claims the draft leaves unused, each of which hardens the design it commits to: (1) NVMe device self-test support is OPTIONAL per drive — an Intel 600p reports 'Device Self-test Not Supported' (oacs bit 4, edstt/dsto = 0) despite 'health: healthy', so the draft's 'inheriting smartd's scheduling and self-test logic free' silently inherits nothing on such drives and the hook design needs the capability check; (2) go-hass-agent's field evidence shows SMART data arriving as ATTRIBUTES on disk entities rather than separate entities (forcing template-sensor extraction) and being absent on Raspberry Pi OS despite x86 presence — the entity-vs-attribute surface choice is a live design decision with an incumbent cautionary precedent; (3) the control node /dev/nvme0 accepts SMART ioctls more appropriately than the namespace node /dev/nvme0n1 because SMART is global to the device — concrete targeting for the hook; (4) vendor product-EOL and wear-EOL are distinct signals (a drive at ~1% of rated TBW can already be flagged EOL) — the bridge should expose both, which the binary_sensor framing alone misses.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend §6's SMART paragraph by 2–3 sentences: 'Two caveats the hook design carries: device self-test support is optional per drive (an Intel 600p reports Not Supported via oacs/edstt while still healthy), so the inherited self-test scheduling needs a capability check, not an assumption [[how-to-check-nvme-ssd-health-newbie-corner-arch-linux-forums]]; and the surface decision — separate entities vs attributes on a disk entity — has an incumbent precedent worth avoiding, go-hass-agent exposing SMART as attributes that template sensors must individually surface [[how-to-see-your-ssdhdd-health-directly-in-home-assistant-diy-ideas]]. Expose wear (percentage-used) and vendor product-EOL as distinct sensors: a drive at 1% of rated TBW can already be flagged EOL [[whats-the-best-way-to-monitor-nvme-health-applications-endeavouros]].' Optionally add control-node (/dev/nvme0) targeting to §5.C's bullet [[answers]].

findings.location: §5.D 'Secrets wiring is unchanged: sops-nix (the fleet's secrets-decryption module) decrypts to /run/secrets with per-secret owner and restartUnits, so sops.secrets.mqtt_ha_linux_agent.owner = "io" works identically for a system service.' — no citation on the sentence
findings.finding: A load-bearing Phase-2 claim (the pallene secrets decision and the entire 'wiring unchanged' position hang off it) is asserted with zero provenance while the vault holds exactly the evidence: sops-nix's system module decrypts to non-persistent /run/secrets with per-secret owner/group and restartUnits — the mechanism the sentence states — plus the contrast that justifies 'unchanged' rather than merely asserting it: the home-manager module runs as a systemd USER service placing secrets in $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/secrets.d with consumer services required to order after it, i.e. the user-service secrets path the design is retiring. Under this run's deep-inference directive, a derived claim that fails to name the sourced claims it derives from is a flag; this is the clearest instance in the draft.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the wikilink to the sops-nix note on that sentence and one clause carrying the contrast: '...works identically for a system service [[github-mic92sops-nix-atomic-secret-provisioning-for-nixos-based-on-sops-github]] — per-secret owner and restartUnits are the system-module semantics, while the home-manager path the retired user unit would have depended on runs as a user service into $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/secrets.d with ordering requirements, so the system-service move lands on the simpler of the two documented shapes.'

findings.location: §7 'The sandbox-legality proof, from the Nix source itself.' paragraph (cites only the goal.cc loopback comment and the mosquitto man page)
findings.finding: The draft's sandbox-legality proof rests on mechanism (the Nix source's private-loopback comment) and leaves unused the corpus's two EMPIRICAL precedents that turn mechanism into practice: nixpkgs PR #283878, a real merged derivation whose checkPhase ran a localhost HTTP server + client pair inside the build sandbox (the nixpkgs-review build log shows 'Serving HTTP on 127.0.0.1 port 8000 ... GET / HTTP/1.1 200'), and the NixOS Discourse thread where the same author demonstrated the cross-boundary shape FAILING — a server started outside the build is unreachable from checkPhase because 'there are different loopback interfaces in different namespaces'. The second precedent is the evidence for exactly the design decision the draft asserts without support: why the harness must spawn mosquitto inside the test rather than reuse a host broker. A gate-design chapter that cites merged-PR practice plus the failed alternative is materially stronger than one citing the source comment alone, and both notes were fetched precisely for this ladder step (tagged gap-04).
findings.suggested_fix: In §7's sandbox-legality paragraph, after the goal.cc sentence, insert: 'Practice confirms the mechanism on both sides: merged nixpkgs PR #283878 ran a localhost server-client pair inside checkPhase — the build log shows "Serving HTTP on 127.0.0.1 port 8000" serving requests from the test client [[single-file-cli-init-at-1149-by-n8henrie-pull-request-283878-nixosnixpkgs-github]] — while the same author's Discourse thread shows the cross-boundary shape failing: a server outside the build is unreachable, different loopback interfaces in different namespaces, which is precisely why the harness spawns mosquitto inside the test instead of reusing a host broker [[local-networking-in-checkphase-help-nixos-discourse]].'

findings.location: §8 Phase 1 exit criteria (one-shot live kiosk restart test) and §2.C's broker-side $SYS drop-counter check
findings.finding: The corpus holds the MQTT blackbox round-trip probe pattern — publish/subscribe round-trip on a single topic as the definition of a completed probe, with message loss observable as a published-minus-received counter delta and hangs as started-minus-completed, per the inovex mqtt_blackbox_exporter metric semantics, plus the Netdata supervision docs for such exporters — and the draft uses none of it. The supervisor's exit criteria end at a one-shot manual restart test and the $SYS counter is broker-side only; a standing client-side round-trip self-probe is the difference between 'fixed once' and 'verifiably never silent again', converting deafness from an incident into an alarm. The exporter itself need not ship to the fleet (no Prometheus there); the corpus evidence is the design pattern, implementable inside the agent or as an HA automation.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to §8 Phase 1's exit criteria (or the forward-looking paragraph): 'Beyond the one-shot restart test, a standing publish/subscribe round-trip self-probe — the blackbox-exporter pattern where loss is a published-minus-received delta and a hang is started-minus-completed [[github-inovexmqtt_blackbox_exporter-prometheus-exporter-for-mqtt-monitoring-gith]] — turns deafness from an incident into an alarm, implementable inside the agent or as an HA automation with no extra exporter.'

findings.location: Exec preamble (the ~570-word single-paragraph 'The answer first' opener), §8 opening line, Opinionated Synthesis first paragraph, §4.D scope-discipline paragraph
findings.finding: Bloat check B1. The report measures 63.1KB — above the 45–55KB top-performer band and approaching the 65–70KB bottom-performer band. The dilution is concentrated in thesis restatement rather than padded prose: the ordered-plan thesis appears in full argumentative form at least four times (exec preamble: 'The order is non-negotiable: fix reliability first, deploy fleet-wide second, add features third'; §4.D: 'fix the lifecycle, keep the sensor surface deliberately minimal... spend features only where jupiterOS consumes them'; §8: 'The order is the argument: nothing else is observable while the agent is deaf'; synthesis: 'reliability first (Phase 0–1...), fleet second (Phase 2...), features third (Phase 3...)'). The two-bugs mechanics are explained completely twice (§2.B's mechanical walkthrough and the synthesis's first paragraph, which re-narrates subscribe-once, the swallowed ConnAck, rumqttc's contract, and the three traps with only phrasing variation). The exec preamble also pre-argues the full adoption dialectic ('Adoption is the wrong move — the fleet's deciding features are exactly what no incumbent can express — and the strongest case for it is engaged at full strength below and answered on evidence') that §4 then argues for 2,000 words.
findings.evidence: Draft measured at 63,154 bytes; passages located at line 3 (exec preamble), §8 opener (line 188), Opinionated Synthesis first paragraph (line 202)
findings.suggested_fix: Tighten three passages without losing evidence: (1) cut the Opinionated Synthesis's first paragraph to its verdict sentence plus a one-clause mechanism recap — §2 already carries the full mechanics and the synthesis re-derives them; (2) reduce §8's opener from a three-clause mini-argument to a single sentence ('The order is the argument, and each phase's exit criteria feed the next gate.'); (3) trim the exec preamble's adoption preview to one clause ('adoption is answered at full strength in §4 and fails on packaging and expressibility'). Together this removes roughly 600–900 words of repetition and pulls the report back toward the top-performer band.

findings.location: Exec preamble final sentences vs Opinionated Synthesis final sentences
findings.finding: Bloat check B2. Exec: 'The order is non-negotiable: fix reliability first, deploy fleet-wide second... add features third. Adoption is the wrong move — the fleet's deciding features are exactly what no incumbent can express'. Synthesis close: 'reliability first (Phase 0–1...), fleet second (Phase 2...), features third (Phase 3...). ... The fleet's deciding features are exactly what both the agent incumbents and the monitoring incumbents cannot express'. The thesis sentences repeat near-verbatim — 'the fleet's deciding features are exactly what' is word-for-word, and the three-phase ordering restates with the same key phrases — well over the 50% phrase-overlap threshold, inflating length without adding value.
findings.evidence: Draft line 3 (exec preamble) and line 204 (synthesis final paragraph)
findings.suggested_fix: Differentiate the synthesis's close: replace the repeated 'deciding features' sentence with forward-looking content the exec preamble lacks — the standing-watch flip conditions already in §8's forward-looking paragraph (a released upstream reconnect signal, an incumbent shipping select-with-state-sync or a NixOS module, an end-to-end v5 decision) restated as the named reopen-triggers, or the 6–12-month observation-plane framing — so the report ends on implications rather than a re-quotation of its own opening.
